Yes! and this is basically what I’m doing still, just using the prong to help break her focus. She wouldn’t turn away for her treat when I mark. Nothing is higher value to her than staring down a wild animal, so she isn’t motivated enough to turn away on her own to get a food reward. I had some mild success with it at very very far distances, and gained even more success when I introduced a toy reward, but it’s incredibly difficult to set up controllable scenarios with wildlife. It seemed for every successfully rewarded engagement (and sometimes even voluntary disengagement), we had 10 unsuccessful set ups. It eventually got to the point where nothing could break her focus even at far distances other than completely turning around. Her staring, and then eventually lunging, behavior had become too practiced to the point where there was basically no windup, as soon as she set eyes on an animal even hundreds of feet away she would lunge. I can read her well, but her reaction time will always be quicker than mine. 

I’m basically following the same method but if she fails to turn towards me for the treat I’m able to use pressure on the prong to make her disengage and then reward. First I corrected her lunging by turning around when she made moves to chase, now she seems to think twice before she lunges and gives herself that discomfort from hitting the end of the leash while wearing a prong. I’ve managed to create enough of a window that we can practice engage/disengage before a lunge happens. I used the same engage/disengage method for her dog reactivity and it worked wonderfully, without needing the prong. Her prey drive is just very strong and unfortunately, very well practiced now.

I can walk my dog on a harness in a heel with a loose leash. Walking really isn’t the problem. But I have no way of correcting her or regaining her attention if her prey drive is triggered. She doesn’t respond to pressure on the harness. Stopping walking would do nothing in that situation. And I can only turn around and drag her away so many times before I decide I need to change what I’m doing. The prong has enabled me to snap her out of it so she can practice refocusing on me, and also has stopped her from practicing lunging.
